records.capability: Typed durable assistant partial-progress frame encoder and reducer
records.ts_comparison: Rust has versioned, identity-bearing frames with ordered block starts/deltas/ends, scalar text offsets, checkpoints and validated replay. The historical TS assistant-message-frame module referenced in its comments is absent from the reviewed TS inventory; SESSION-029/031 full-message JSONL and RPC-004/013 transient projections do not establish this frame persistence contract. Preserve it. The frame enum does not encode terminal usage/stop metadata, so this is a durable partial-progress capability rather than complete settled-message metadata persistence.

records.capability: Explicit failure when an assistant result producer disappears
records.ts_comparison: The native unbounded MPSC event stream pairs with a oneshot result; a dropped result producer yields RecvError. The TS helper can end iteration with an undefined result while leaving result() unresolved. Preserve native producer-drop failure while adding the TS stream/error dispatch contracts.

records.capability: Operational native AgentHarness versus the exported TypeScript v2 scaffold
records.ts_comparison: The directly compared TypeScript packages/agent AgentHarness methods explicitly reject or return static no-op results, while Rust creates a working durable main-lane runner. This is scoped to that exported class, not a claim that the TypeScript coding-agent cannot run sessions.

records.capability: Orphan-tool repair inside the harness converter
records.ts_comparison: The Rust converter synthesizes missing provider-context results without rerunning tools and drops unmatched results. The directly compared TS harness converter only maps roles; related repair in other TS layers remains a separate audit dependency.

records.capability: Native execution-environment improvements to retain
records.ts_comparison: Rust offers an explicit per-call shell-program override and filters inherited host-private variables. The directly compared NodeExecutionEnv selects its configured Bash-like shell and spreads inherited environment variables without that filter. Keep these native features while fixing the inheritEnv=false and pipe-draining defects.

records.capability: Native filesystem search/listing through ExecutionEnv
records.ts_comparison: TS default find and grep provision fd/rg; Rust traverses and matches in process. Preserve that backend choice while implementing TOOLS-028/029/030 observable semantics.

records.capability: MutatingEnv capability boundary and queue held through mutation I/O

records.capability: Native image processing without Photon worker/WASM
records.ts_comparison: The Rust image backend can remain native; its corrected orientation-aware no-transform condition is valuable. TOOLS-023 separates backend choice from MIME/quality/resize/coordinate differences.

records.capability: Additional edit input compatibility and duplicate-match context
records.ts_comparison: Rust accepts single edit objects and JSON-string objects and returns richer ambiguity context; current TS normalizes legacy flat input and JSON array strings. Preserve intentional Rust compatibility while fixing exact precedence.

records.capability: Optional Windows PowerShell tool
records.ts_comparison: Outside the seven-name TS factories inspected here, Rust exports a Windows-only PowerShell tool using UTF-16LE base64 EncodedCommand, fixed noninteractive options and capture cancellation/timeout. Preserve it; this is a factory comparison, not a claim that no TS extension can supply PowerShell.

records.capability: Bounded native blocking RPC writer
records.ts_comparison: Retain the 64-message channel, blocking sink isolation, ordered drain and failure cancellation while adding the distinct TOOLS-031 byte-budget/isolation contract.

records.capability: Native v4 mutation log and durable lane operations

records.ts_comparison: Rust limits retained handles and active/cleanup work separately to 16 each, reserves before await, and keeps an active permit until execution scopes actually become idle after the 2 s cleanup grace. records.capability: Lifetime-bounded delta/final output and owner-checked destructive polling
records.ts_comparison: Native output budget counts delta plus final bytes cumulatively (4 MiB/8192 events), regardless of polling; result is withheld until queued deltas drain. One oversized first delta may exceed the 64 KiB per-poll target. Retain lifetime bounds alongside new nondestructive artifacts.

records.capability: Invocation/plugin lifetime cancellation and fail-closed panic handling
records.ts_comparison: Native children are linked to invocation, parent run, parent scope and explicit job cancellation/timeout, with expired invocations rejected and revoked owners unable to reenter. records.capability: Exact inherited private provider/model binding and guarded tool scopes

records.capability: Independent native side questions
records.ts_comparison: Native one-turn tool-free side questions use a 64 KiB UTF-8 tail of committed user/assistant text, excluding tool/custom/image/thinking, and survive parent-run cancellation while remaining bounded by session close. This is a distinct capability from TS controllable persistent V2 child views.

records.capability: Monotonic synchronized timing collection
records.ts_comparison: Rust uses Instant, Mutex and a fixed namespace print order; TS uses Date.now and Map insertion order. Preserve monotonic timing even if moving the Rust startup flush earlier.

records.capability: Explicit local span contexts, no-op and in-memory test sinks
records.ts_comparison: Rust supplies a Send+Sync TelemetryContext, RAII span guard, stdout/file/disabled production contexts and an in-memory completion sink. The inspected TS observation subsystem uses event projections rather than this trait/sink contract. Preserve these alongside observation; a separate source-read concurrent-drop defect is documented.

records.capability: Native Cargo artifact installation, ownership locking and rollback to preserve
records.ts_comparison: Retain the Cargo backend, strict mutation registry, artifact ownership checks, lock, staging and rollback when adding resource-package commands. Do not replace them with TS's weaker payload-then-settings ordering. Keep backend-specific registries separate and expose native versus resource-package identities explicitly in the command facade. No new Rust implementation is required for this retained capability; size is zero and compatibility work is counted in the owning source/CLI entries.

records.capability: Verified native extension prebuilt distribution and publisher provenance to preserve
records.ts_comparison: Preserve the bounded manifest/archive protocol, publisher continuity, provenance and object validation while adding TS resource backends. Keep verification before activation and runtime ABI loading after it. No new Rust implementation is estimated for this retained capability. Do not loosen archive/path/hash limits to make TS package naming fit, and do not treat downloaded native libraries as equivalent to JS package directories.

Add resource-package notices through explicit backend-tagged records and shared presentation only after CLI-028 exists. Preserve the distinction between automatic native disable flags and TS explicit update-service behavior. No replacement implementation is required for this retained capability; size is zero.
